terms.gloss: at the right time, in season
at the wrong time, out of season
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.25: accēdere (Lewis & Short s.v. intempestīvus)
Cic. Fam. 11.16: adīre ad aliquem (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Said on someone's arrival: opportūnē, just in time (see in the nick of time).

phrases.latin: Salvum tē advenīre, Dēmea, gaudēmus. — Ehem, opportūnē: tē ipsum quaeritō.
phrases.english: We’re glad to see you safely here, Demea. — Ah, just in time: you’re the very man I’m looking for.

sources: Lewis & Short: tempestivus · Lewis & Short: intempestivus · Lewis & Short: opportune
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 88, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations from the Latīnitās loci collections, checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
